issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the inventory class: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (UML class 'Stock' with methods add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). The template repository instead provides a fully implemented class named 'Inventory' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java) that implements those methods, and also contains an empty 'Stock.java' file. The solution implementation uses 'Inventory' as the type of the shared stock (SealSaloon has a static Inventory stock). This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory, plus an empty Stock.java) confuses students about which class name to follow, which file to modify or implement, and whether to adhere to the UML (Stock) or the provided template (Inventory).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the inventory class name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Rename Inventory.java to Stock.java (update class name, file name and all references in template and solution to 'Stock') so it matches the UML and problem text, and remove the empty Stock.java if it would conflict; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock' and remove the empty Stock.java file from the template repository. Ensure SealSaloon, the UML, and all example code consistently reference the same class name and that only one canonical file (Inventory.java or Stock.java) is provided in the template.

issues.description: The exercise text and UML refer to a core class named 'Stock' (the saloon's inventory/stock of ingredients). However, the provided code (both template and solution) implements this concept with a class named 'Inventory' (class Inventory in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java). Additionally, the template repository contains an essentially empty Stock.java file, increasing confusion. Students reading the problem will look for a 'Stock' class and its methods as shown in the UML, but the codebase exposes 'Inventory' instead; this naming mismatch makes it difficult to map the problem requirements (Stock: add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock) to the actual implementation and may block or confuse learners when they attempt to implement or call the expected class and methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier for the shared inventory concept across all artifacts. Two acceptable remedies: (A) Rename the Inventory class and its file to Stock (Inventory.java -> Stock.java), update all references in the codebase (e.g., SealSaloon.getStock() return type and static field), and remove the empty template Stock.java placeholder; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock' and remove the empty template Stock.java to avoid duplication. Option A (renaming Inventory -> Stock in code and removing the empty Stock.java) is recommended to match the original UML wording.
